name: Imagify
summary: Image compression and WebP and AVIF conversion for WordPress, through a plugin that also bulk-optimises an existing media library; plans are metered by megabytes of images a month.
best_for: WordPress site owners with image-heavy pages, such as blogs, stores and portfolios, who want images compressed and converted to WebP or AVIF by a plugin instead of by hand
skip_if: your site is not on WordPress; your host, CDN or theme already compresses and converts images; or you add only a few images a month and the free quota or a manual tool covers it
honest_knock: A prepaid yearly plan is not refunded. The free tier's 20MB a month and 2MB per image are only enough for a test, Growth charges $5 for each extra GB, and Infinite's unlimited use falls under a fair-use clause. In our test on 21 October 2026 the free quota counted the original file size, not the compressed result (a 11.8KB and a 48.9KB image moved the counter to 61.44KB), a 3.4MB file was refused at the 2MB cap without using quota, and the 'You saved' total on the web app's optimizer page showed the size after compression instead of the saving; the History page had the right figures.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Growth · per month, billed yearly, excluding tax
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-17 in a browser on imagify.io/pricing in the yearly view, with the monthly rates read on the same page on 15 October 2026; the terms name US dollars, excluding tax) Starter is $0 a month: 20MB a month, about 200 images, unlimited websites, 2MB maximum per image, no credit card. Growth is $4.99 a month billed yearly, or $5.99 billed monthly: 500MB a month, about 5,000 images, unlimited websites and upload size, and $5 for each additional GB. Infinite is $9.99 a month billed yearly, or $11.99 monthly: unlimited images, websites and upload size at no extra cost, subject to the fair-use clause in the terms. The page advertises two months free on yearly billing but does not show the yearly invoice total. The terms rule out a refund on a prepaid twelve-month subscription. You cancel from the Billing page, and images already optimised stay optimised.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on the free plan in Imagify's web app: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We uploaded three of our own simple test images (a 12 KB PNG, a 50 KB JPG and a 3.4 MB PNG), compared Smart and Lossless and watched the quota counter after each step.
findings: The account started at '0.0KB / 20MB used. You have 100% credit left.' Auto-converting PNG to JPEG is marked 'only for Pro users'; resizing is available on free.
Smart compression took the PNG from 11.8KB to 3.3KB (72.36%) and the JPG from 48.9KB to 12.3KB (74.91%), each within about 8 seconds.

After the first two images the quota counter read 61.44KB of 20MB, much closer to their input sizes than to the compressed results. The later counter increments varied, so we did not establish the exact quota accounting rule.
Lossless took the same PNG from 11.8KB to 5.8KB (51.05%), against 3.3KB with Smart.
The 3.4MB file was refused straight away with 'File size must be under 2.0 MB. Current file size is 3.4 MB' and used no quota.

The summary on the optimizer page is mislabelled: 'You saved 15.5KB out of 60.7KB' gave the size after compression (3.3KB + 12.3KB), while the real saving was about 45KB. The History page showed the right saving per file.
History notes 'Optimized images are available to download for 24 hours' on a free account. End state: 92.16KB of 20MB used after four optimisations and one refused upload.
